value.rationale: Minimum-support circuits are a natural invariant of the exact node relation configuration: they identify the smallest groups of conifold nodes capable of participating in a global relation. The initiating paper uses the same relation matrix to study smoothability, while the broader conifold-relation theory identifies such lattices with exceptional-curve and mirror vanishing-sphere relations. The complete result that the minimum support is three and occurs in exactly five primitive ways is therefore structurally motivated, finite, and reusable rather than an arbitrary slice. It sharpens the node subsystem from global rank/coloop data to its smallest interaction patterns without overstating consequences for the four additional cone points.
